title: Robot Assembly Line Energy Simulator
description: A physics-inspired simulation where a robot arm operates on an assembly line, picking up and placing interpolation test objects onto conveyor platforms. The user controls the robot's joint angles, gripper force, and conveyor speed while maintaining energy conservation across the system. An undo/redo history allows reverting any configuration step.
prompt: Create a single HTML file using Three.js r170 that implements a robot assembly line energy conservation simulator. Load both GLB assets using GLTFLoader from a CDN. Place the robot model at the center of the scene on a raised platform. Place the InterpolationTest model scaled to 0.4 as a manipulable workpiece on a conveyor track to the robot's left. Camera: perspective at position (5, 4, 6) looking at origin, with OrbitControls. Lighting: one directional light casting shadows, one hemisphere light for ambient fill, and a point light on the robot arm tip. Create a flat ground plane with grid texture. Build a UI panel (HTML overlay, top-right) with these controls: (1) three sliders for robot joint rotation angles (base yaw, shoulder pitch, elbow pitch) each -180 to 180 degrees that animate the robot's first three child bone rotations, (2) a gripper force slider 0-100 that scales the InterpolationTest object between 0.3-0.5 to simulate compression, (3) a conveyor speed slider that translates the InterpolationTest along the X axis over time, (4) a gravity toggle button that enables/disables downward drift on the workpiece, (5) an energy display showing kinetic plus potential energy computed as KE=0.5*mass*velocity^2 and PE=mass*g*height where mass is derived from gripper force, (6) Undo and Redo buttons. Implement a state history system: every time any slider changes or a button is pressed, push the full state (all slider values, object positions, toggle states) onto an undo stack and clear the redo stack. Undo pops from undo stack to redo stack and restores state. Redo reverses this. The energy display must update each animation frame and the total system energy should remain approximately constant when gravity is on and conveyor moves (convert PE loss to KE gain). Animate the robot's interpolation channels if present. Require at least 10-14 distinct interaction steps to fully configure and test the system: adjust three joints, set gripper force, set conveyor speed, toggle gravity, observe energy, undo two steps, redo one step, readjust a joint, and toggle gravity again. Display step count in the UI. Use requestAnimationFrame for the render loop.
